**Subject: Executive Briefing proposal for Tamarack Instruments**

Dear Dana Whitfield,

**Situation**
Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It has about 1,100 staff and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has a customer service chatbot deployed on its support portal and is piloting AI visual inspection on the German production line. It plans to introduce AI sales forecasting next year. Your stated objective is clear: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." Two stated constraints apply. Customer data must stay in the EU, and the German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

**What the Briefing covers for the Client**
The Briefing maps the EU AI Act and GDPR to each use case. It presents these as expectations to verify with counsel, not as legal advice. For the chatbot, it reviews the expectation that people are informed they are interacting with an AI system. For visual inspection, it examines how the system may be classified under the EU AI Act and whether a GDPR data protection impact assessment is expected. One question will be confirmed at intake: whether the system touches production staff and so engages the works council. For forecasting, it sets out the authorization questions to answer before build begins. United States obligations appear only as a general landscape item.

The operating model overview uses the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen). The board layer draws on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards). The session is anchored in three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human. ISO/IEC 42001 work is targeted for next year, although no start date is fixed. The session shows how early governance choices can align with that standard. It does not promise certification or any audit outcome.

**Logistics and price**
The Briefing is a two-hour live virtual session priced at US$3,000. The session date and attendee list will be confirmed at intake. The roles identified are General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors.

**What the Client receives afterward**
The Client receives a follow-up memo. It summarizes the decisions surfaced and our readiness observations. It also sets out three prioritized recommendations, each mapped to a next program option.

**Next step**
The decision timeline is not yet known. We propose a short intake call to confirm the session date, the attendees and the works council question above.

Kind regards,

Senior AI Governance Consultant
AI Governance Academy
